reighard1901.cite: Reighard J. & Jennings H.S. (1901) Anatomy of the Cat. Henry Holt, New York. Alimentary canal: the mouth pp. 221-230
says: p. 224: the adult cat has thirty teeth, fourteen in the lower jaw and sixteen in the upper jaw; twelve incisors, four canines, ten premolars, four molars (formula i 3/3, c 1/1, pm 3/2, m 1/1)
p. 225: incisors small, the crown edge notched into three minute cusps, one fang; the lateral incisors are the largest, upper larger than lower
p. 225: canines long, strong, pointed, one fang, one cusp

p. 225: upper pm1 (modern P2) small, single cusp and fang; pm2 (P3) a large central cusp, one smaller cranial and two small caudal cusps; pm3 (P4) the largest tooth, three large cusps in longitudinal series, three fangs
pp. 225-226: the upper molar is small and lies caudomediad of the last premolar; two small cusps, two fangs

p. 226: lower premolars similar, the caudal one a little larger, each four cusps (one large, a small one craniad, two small caudad), two fangs; the lower molar is the largest lower tooth, two large cusps, two fangs
p. 221: the mouth cavity extends from the lips to the pharynx, narrower toward the lips, broadening caudad as far back as the last teeth
p. 222: the mucosa of the hard palate is raised into seven or eight curved transverse ridges, concave caudad, with rows of papillae between them
p. 223: the sides of the mouth cavity are formed by the teeth and the gums

pp. 226-228: tongue elongated, flat above, broadest in the middle; ventral surface and lateral borders smooth and free of papillae; dorsum papillate with a slight median furrow; filiform papillae, many horny and tooth-like with points turned caudad, most numerous at the middle of the free end; circumvallate papillae in a V with the apex caudad
p. 230: the soft palate is the free curtain forming the caudal part of the roof, ending caudad in a free arched border
reighard1901.confidence: high (primary anatomy text, read this session)

merck_wright.cite: Wright A. (Cornell). Dentition and Dental Nomenclature of Animals. Merck Veterinary Manual (digestive system / dental development and anatomy)
merck_wright.says: cats have only one molar in each quadrant (109, 209, 309, 409); footnote: the maxillary second premolar and the maxillary first molar can be absent in some cats
merck_wright.confidence: high for the formula (agrees with Reighard 1901: two independent sources)
